subject: hero shrew
title: A Man Stood on This Shrew for Five Minutes. It Walked Away

scenes.text: A man stood on this shrew. It walked away.
In 1910, in the Congo, locals showed a visiting scientist their party trick. A 70 kilogram man stood on a hero shrew for five minutes.
The shrew weighs about 50 grams, the same as a golf ball. Any other mammal that size would be crushed in a second.
The secret is its spine. You have five lumbar vertebrae. The hero shrew has ten or eleven, and they interlock, bone on bone, like armour.
For its size, that backbone is four times more robust than any other mammal's. Scientists think it uses it as a crowbar, levering up logs to reach beetle grubs.
The Mangbetu people wore its dried body as a charm for invincibility. For once, the legend was tested, and it held.

description:
A 70 kilogram man stood on a hero shrew for five minutes, and it walked away unharmed.
The hero shrew of the Congo Basin weighs about 50 grams but has 10 to 11 interlocking lumbar vertebrae instead of the usual five, giving it a spine about four times more robust for its size than any other mammal's. The demonstration was first recorded by a Western scientist in 1910; a second species, Scutisorex thori, was described in 2013. Researchers think the shrew uses its back as a lever to lift logs and reach beetle grubs.
What other tiny animal has a record-breaking body part?
thumbnail_text: A MAN STOOD ON IT. IT LIVED
first_comment: A second hero shrew species was only described in 2013, with a slightly simpler spine, so the back was still evolving. Which animal superpower should we cover next?
